ai.description: This species reaches 1.2 meters. It features a grey to brown body with dark rhomboid markings and a distinctively broad, viper-like head. It lacks the compressed, paddle-like tail of other sea snakes.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Viperine Sea Snake is best identified by its distinctively small, blunt head and a series of large, dark, diamond-shaped dorsal blotches that narrow toward the tail.
ai.habitat: *Hydrophis viperinus* inhabits the coastal waters of the Indian subcontinent, typically frequenting shallow, muddy-bottomed marine environments and river estuaries.
ai.behavior: The Viperine sea snake is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively hunting for bottom-dwelling fish along the seafloor in shallow coastal waters.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hydrophis viperinus* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to live young. It typically produces a small litter of 2–4 offspring, with breeding occurring during the monsoon.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hydrophis viperinus* occurs along the western and eastern coasts of the Indian subcontinent, primarily inhabiting shallow coastal waters and estuaries at sea level.
